summary: A former ground lookout on the 8,999-ft Sentinel Peak in the Chiricahuas; the lookout is long gone, with a foundation and a plaque still visible on the summit.

facts.status_note: Lookout removed; a foundation and a metal plaque remain on the summit, per a trail guide

access.note: Reached on foot by Crest Trail #270C from Junction Saddle, then a 420-foot spur to the summit. The trail beyond South Fork has not been surveyed for several years and its conditions are unknown.

notes_for_editor: No built date and no removal date were found in any source read, so the story gives neither. The 1945 staffing comes from a newspaper report quoted on westlookouts, not from a primary scan. Two accounts describe the summit remains: a trail guide (foundation and plaque) and a 2019 hiking blog (trash and a foundation); they agree on a foundation. Do not confuse with Tucson's Sentinel Peak (A Mountain, Pima County), which has a hmdb.org historical marker; that is a different site and was not used. Record coordinates (31.81481, -109.23819) sit within about 0.004 degrees of longitude of the trail guide's junction coordinates (31.81406, -109.24235), so the record's location looks right. Access beyond South Fork is unsurveyed per the trail guide.
